content: 1. Develop and utilize an implementation guide toolkit to monitor the effective integration of the World Health Organization’s (WHO) family planning guidelines into national-level guidance documents, as well as their application at the national, facility, and provider levels. 2. Establish specific goals tailored to the suggested metrics provided for each organizational level, taking into account the context in which the implementation team operates. These metrics are designed to reflect the core components of the guidance across three organizational levels. 3. Create and implement strategies, tools, and processes to systematically collect data on the identified metrics. 4. Gather data and document the outcomes of assessments conducted at each level of implementation. 5. Carefully consider the timing of assessments for certain indicators. For example, ensure that family planning (FP) guidelines, tools, protocols, and training manuals are aligned with the Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) and Selected Practice Recommendations (SPR) metrics. 6. Evaluate MEC adherence by measuring the proportion of eligibility categories that are inconsistent with WHO guidance, the number of medical conditions or contraceptive methods from the MEC that are not included in the country’s FP guidelines, and the number of additional medical conditions or contraceptive methods included in national FP guidelines. 7. Assess SPR adherence by identifying the number of recommendations that are inconsistent with SPR guidance. 8. Set specific goals and targets for outcomes, such as ensuring that updates to MEC and SPR are addressed. Metrics for this include the existence of structured processes for monitoring and addressing WHO FP guidance updates, the time required to update and release country FP guidelines, and the time required to update and release job aids and tools. 9. Support processes at the clinic level by ensuring the presence of structured supervision, audit, and feedback mechanisms. 10. Train providers in the use of national family planning guidance and ensure they are equipped to offer the full spectrum of contraceptive methods. 11. Ensure facilities adhere to national family planning guidelines. Metrics for this include the proportion of providers effectively and fully utilizing FP guidance, the proportion of providers effectively and fully utilizing FP tools, and the proportion of providers trained to deliver at least one long-acting reversible or permanent contraceptive method. 12. Monitor provider adherence to national FP recommendations. For example, assess the proportion of clients receiving MEC category 4 methods, which should generally be very low, as these methods are contraindicated.
